steps: Let the capacitance of the capacitor without dielectric be C_0. Its initial charge is Q_0 = C_0 V_0.
The capacitance of the first capacitor with the dielectric is C_1 = K C_0 = \alpha V C_0.
The charge on the first capacitor at a potential drop V is Q_1 = C_1 V = \alpha C_0 V^2.
The charge on the second capacitor at the same potential drop V is Q_2 = C_0 V.
By conservation of charge, Q_1 + Q_2 = Q_0, which gives \alpha C_0 V^2 + C_0 V = C_0 V_0.
Substituting \alpha = 1 V^{-1} and V_0 = 30 V, we get V^2 + V - 30 = 0. Solving for V > 0 yields V = 5 V.
